text: The loaves didn't multiply in the disciples' hands. Jesus "kept giving" to them, so they had to keep coming back to Him.
explanation:
Jesus took the five loaves and two fish, looked up to heaven, blessed and broke them. Those verbs describe single actions. But "gave them to the disciples" is in a continuous tense: the NLT says He "kept giving the bread and fish to the disciples." The multiplying happened in His hands, and the disciples kept going back to Him again and again.

That's how supply flows today. Last week's time with Him won't cover today's need. Costs may rise, but nothing takes Him by surprise. Keep coming back into His presence; He keeps on giving, and twelve baskets were left over.

text: "There is no one who has left house… for My sake and the gospel's, who shall not receive a hundredfold now in this time."
explanation:
Peter said, "See, we have left all and followed You." Jesus didn't promise poverty. He promised a hundredfold "now in this time": houses, brothers, sisters, mothers, children and lands, with persecutions too, and in the age to come, eternal life.

That's not licence to live for money. "You cannot serve God and mammon." Many who chase wealth sacrifice their children's growing years and their peace for things they enjoy for a few months. Serve Him, and the hundredfold follows; you can never out-give God.

text: "On the third day Abraham lifted his eyes and saw the place." He named it Jehovah Jireh: the Lord will provide.
explanation:
God sent Abraham to "one of the mountains of which I shall tell you." On the third day he saw it: Moriah, whose highest ridge would one day be Calvary. There God provided the ram, and pointed to the Son He would provide.

The third day keeps appearing as a day of supply and healing. To dying Hezekiah God said, "I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tears; surely I will heal you. On the third day you shall go up to the house of the Lord." Every tear you cry, He sees, even the ones you hold back.

text: The ten lepers weren't healed and then sent to the priest. "As they went, they were cleansed."
explanation:
The law sent a leper to the priest only after he was healed. Jesus told ten lepers to go while they were still sick: act as though it's done, and trust My word. On the way, they were made clean. At Cana the servants filled jars with water, and it was as they carried it to the master of the feast that it became wine.

God often withholds the supply until you're moving in faith, because He wants a people who depend on Him daily. Do what He says, and the provision meets you on the road.

text: "By faith Noah prepared an ark for the saving of his household." Every word about Jesus to your children adds a plank.
explanation:
Jesus said the days before His return would be like the days of Noah. Sins people think are new are as old as the flood, just back in fashion. You can't make the world listen, but you can prepare an ark for your house.

Start somewhere. If your children are young, read to them about Jesus. If they're teenagers, ask for one evening a week: "Can I share something from the Bible?" Every conversation and every example is another plank in the ark that will carry your family through.

text: Can't sleep, but you feel alert and fresh, not oppressed? Maybe God wants to talk. Say, "Speak, Lord, I'm listening."
explanation:
God speaks "in a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls upon men… then He opens the ears of men." By day we're often too busy, glued to our phones, to hear Him. Young Samuel heard God's voice three times before Eli taught him to answer, "Speak, Lord, for Your servant hears."

One such sleepless night, Joseph Prince sensed God asking him to take down the paywalls on his sermons so the gospel could go further and faster. It meant giving up his main income. He said yes, and the message has gone further than ever. When you're wide awake at night, ask Him what He's saying.
